newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mostly lower on slow cash trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mostly lower on slow cash trade.

text.p: Continued slow cash trade kept pressure on CME lumber futures after trading technically between chart points early, traders said.
Lumber closed $0.60 per thousand board feet higher to $2.80 lower with July off $0.80 at $384.60 and September off $1.50 at $375.50 per tbf.

Futures rose to technical resistance at $390 per tbf in July and moved down late on reports of continued slow cash trade. Although the cash spruce lumber market was officially quoted higher, actual trades were being done below the mill asking level, traders said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $375 per tbf, up $3 from last Friday and $13 over the last midweek. But private cash sources are putting spruce in the mid $360 level.
